subject: Quantix performance qualification & mutual plan of action
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@quantix.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick post-call recap + next steps

Hi Jamie —

Thanks for the time today. Short recap from our side to make sure we captured the key goals and constraints correctly: 

- Business goal: real-time insights inside Quantix’s analyst UI (live inference on short prompts, ~15-80 tokens) to reduce analyst triage time by ~40%.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 150ms for single-turn calls in US-west (soft), p99 < 250ms (hard).
- Throughput: baseline 250 QPS during business hours, burst to 1.2k QPS for peak batch runs.
- Model: prefer a high-quality open decoder (we discussed Llama-2 and variants), need to validate accuracy vs distilled 30B.
- Data constraints: all inference for production must run within Quantix VPC / private deployment (sensitive customer PII).
- Ops: Quantix wants rollout in 6–8 weeks, starting with a small PoC that validates latency and token-cost.

Outstanding asks from your team:
- Provide representative workload (sample prompt distribution + traffic shape) — you mentioned sending that today.
- Confirm SLOs and the set of queries that must be low-latency vs batch.

Next steps we propose:
1) SE deep-dive (60–90m) to map topology & run initial perf benchmark (Marissa to lead).
2) Provide PoC checklist + data schema for ingestion (attached).
3) Redwood to run an internal rough-cost estimate and an initial topology sketch for a private deployment.

I’ve attached a one-page SLO matrix with what we discussed; Marissa will follow up with technical details and a deployment sketch. If this aligns, can we lock the SE deep-dive for Tue 2026-11-30 10:00 PT?

Thanks —
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Connor —

Thanks for the summary, that looks right. A couple clarifications:
- P95 of 150ms is our minimum for the interactive desktop path; we can tolerate up to ~400ms for non-critical background enrichment.
- Model decision: we want the PoC to evaluate two variants — a full 70B open model (accuracy priority) and a quantized 30B (cost priority). If cost delta is >2.5x with similar accuracy, we’ll favor the 30B.
- We’ll send a 48-hour sample of prompts and traffic curve by EOD today.

Attachments: I uploaded the sample prompt set and the internal SLO doc (see attachment stub below).

Attachment stubs: quantix-sample-prompts.json (12MB, redacted), quantix-internal-slo.pdf (1.2MB)

Tue 11/30 10:00 PT works for the SE deep-dive — confirm if Marissa needs any infra access ahead of time.

Best,

- Validate p95/p99 targets based on expected cold-start and KV-cache hit rates.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@quantix.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: SE deep-dive recap: topology, perf targets, and PoC checklist

Hi Jamie / Connor —

Thanks again for the deep-dive yesterday. Below is a concise technical recap plus action items for the PoC kickoff.

Summary of perf requirements (confirmed):
- Interactive path: target p95 < 150ms (US-west), p99 < 300ms.
- Background enrichment: target p95 < 500ms.
- Sustained throughput: 250 QPS (business hours), burst up to 1.2k QPS (10m windows).

Model / inference choices:
- Candidate A: Llama-2-70B (FP16) — expected best accuracy, target baseline for correctness tests.
- Candidate B: Distilled/quantized 30B (int8) — target for cost sensitivity testing.
- We’ll run identical eval prompts and measure token-level latency, output divergence (BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics), and per-request token cost.

Suggested private deployment topology (initial PoC):
- Private control plane in Quantix VPC (Redwood Private).
- Two model pools in-us-west-2:
  - Pool 1 (low-latency): 2x A100-80GB, pinned for Llama-2-70B, with 32GB cache warmers and continuous batching disabled for ultra-low tail latency (prefer small batch=1, dynamic KV caching).
  - Pool 2 (economy): 4x A100-40GB (or equivalent T4/RTX if constrained) running quantized 30B with batch windows and relaxed latency SLOs.
- Smart routing policy: route interactive traffic to Pool 1 with fallback to Pool 2 under overload.

Benchmark plan and metrics to collect:
- Run 3 benchmark passes for both models: cold start, warmed KV-cache baseline, and high-concurrency burst.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, GPU utilization, memory headroom, token-cost [$ / 1k tokens].

PoC checklist & deliverables (for kickoff):
- Quantix: provide sanitized prompt set + traffic curve (received), a representative dataset for accuracy eval (N=5k).
- Quantix infra contact for VPC access or confirmation that Redwood can provision a short-term cluster in your VPC (name/email).
- Redwood: initial topology diagram (attached), run benchmark scripts, and produce an ops runbook for failover routing.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-topology.png, quantix-slo-matrix.xlsx, poc-data-schema.csv

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0: infra access & dataset handoff
- Week 1: benchmark & baseline accuracy runs
- Week 2: PoC tuning, routing config, & cost analysis
- Week 3: PoC wrap + recommendation (scale/readiness + next-step contract sketch)

Open questions:
1) Access model for training/benchmark VPC — do you want a short-lived access token or an ops-runner account?
2) Any encryption/HSM requirements beyond KMS at-rest for model artifacts?

If that all looks good we can lock the kickoff for next Monday (2026-11-29) morning PT.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
